title: Unseen Passage (Apathit Gadya)
tagline: An unseen passage of about 250 words answered in Hindi: how to read it, answer from it, and practise on one.

sourceNote.boardprep: All notes, model openings, practice passages, vocabulary, questions and answers on this page are original BoardPrep material written against the CISCE ICSE Examination Year 2028 second-language syllabus registered for this subject. The names, addresses and institutions used in the models are fictional, and the practice passage is BoardPrep’s own writing rather than any prescribed or previously used text.

overview.intro: The syllabus records this task in exact terms: a passage of about 250 words that you have not seen before, with the questions on it answered in Hindi to test understanding of its content. Nothing in that statement invites interpretation beyond the passage — the task is to read accurately, locate what the question asks, and write it back in your own correct Hindi. This chapter treats the task as a method with fixed stages: a survey read that finds the shape of the passage, a targeted second read that locates evidence, a mental map of the question types that appear on passages of this length, and a checking habit that ties every answer back to a line you can point at. Because you cannot practise on a text that is unseen, the fifth lesson carries an original practice passage written for this page, with worked answers you can verify against it line by line.

learningOutcomes: State what the syllabus records about the length, language and purpose of this task.
Survey an unseen passage once for shape and structure before reading for detail.
Distinguish the common question types — factual, vocabulary, reference, summary and inference.
Answer from the passage only, in complete Hindi sentences tied to the line of evidence.
Check every finished answer against the passage line by line before moving on.

learn.title: What the syllabus records about this task

blocks.text: The syllabus statement is precise about three things and silent about the rest, and it is worth reading in that spirit. It gives the length — a passage of about 250 words; it gives the language of the answers — Hindi; and it gives the purpose — understanding of the content. It does not fix the number of questions, the subject of the passage or the exact question forms, which is why this task cannot be rehearsed by topic and can only be rehearsed by method. Every passage will be new; the reading you bring to it is not. What follows in this chapter is that reading: how to take the shape of a page in one pass, how to find the evidence a question needs, and how to write what you found in Hindi that is complete, accurate and answerable only from the passage in front of you.

blocks.caption: What is recorded, and how to prepare for each part

Answer in complete Hindi sentences, not in fragments or a mix of languages

Not fixed in the 2028 syllabus text
Practise varied question forms so no shape of question is unfamiliar

learn.title: The first read: find the shape before the detail

items: Survey first: read the opening and closing sentences of each paragraph to learn what the passage is about and how it moves.
Mark the structure silently — where the facts sit, where an opinion sits, where the numbers and names cluster.
Note the topic in three words in your mind: the passage is about a fair, an argument, a process — that label is your anchor.
On the second, targeted read, stop at each question’s subject and mark the line that answers it before you begin writing.
Budget the two reads deliberately: the first buys orientation, the second buys evidence, and neither is wasted.

blocks.text: Candidates who read for detail first lose the shape of the passage and then lose time hunting for it again: every question sends them back to re-read the whole page. The survey read prevents that by giving you an anchor — you know where the account of the event sits, where the reason is stated and where the result, so each question becomes a visit to one place rather than a search of the whole. The second read is different in kind: it is not for understanding the passage but for pinning the evidence, line by line against the questions. Two reads with different jobs beat three confused ones, and the discipline of stopping the first read when its job is done is what keeps the timing intact.

learn.title: The shapes a question can take

items.meaning: Asks for something the passage states directly — a number, a name, a sequence — with nothing added.
items.context: How many books were placed at the exhibition? The figure is printed in one line.

items.meaning: Asks what a word means as it is used in this passage, which may differ from its general sense.
items.context: The meaning is fixed by the sentence around it, not by the dictionary alone.

items.meaning: Asks what a particular sentence or expression intends — what it means here.
items.context: Answer by restating the sentence in plainer words from its own context.

items.meaning: Asks for the essence of a paragraph or of the passage in brief.
items.context: Keep the events and drop the decoration: who did what, and with what result.

items.meaning: Asks what follows from the passage without being stated outright in one line.
items.context: Stay inside the passage — an inference it cannot support is a guess, not an answer.

blocks.text: Naming the question type before answering it is a small step that changes the answer, because each type has its own discipline. A factual question wants the passage’s own figure or name, copied exactly — no rounding, no substitution from your general knowledge. A vocabulary question is answered from the sentence the word sits in, so read around it before committing a meaning. A reference question restates in plain Hindi what the line means in context. A summary keeps the load-bearing facts and drops the decoration, and an inference walks only as far as the passage walks. Most wrong answers on this task come from answering a different type than the one asked — giving a general truth to a factual question, or a copied line to a summary — so the first second of each answer should be spent deciding what kind of answer it wants.

learn.title: Writing the answer: from evidence to sentence

items: Answer from the passage only: if the answer is not there or cannot be drawn from what is there, you have misread the question or the page.
Write complete Hindi sentences rather than fragments — a bare figure answers fewer of the words the question asks.
Take the key wording from the passage and reshape it into your sentence, which keeps accuracy and shows the understanding the task tests.
Number the parts when the question has parts, and answer them in the order asked, so nothing is missed under time.
Copy numbers, dates and names exactly as printed; a figure that is nearly right is still wrong on the page.
Keep every answer at the depth asked: one line for a one-line question, and no essay where a sentence suffices.

blocks.text: The finished answer has to do two jobs at once: be true to the passage and be written as Hindi that a reader can follow. The safe route between them is evidence first, sentence second — find the line that settles the question, then write that line’s content in your own complete sentence, changing the shape but not the fact. Copying four consecutive lines instead of answering shows the passage but not your reading of it, while answering from memory or from the subject generally risks stating something the passage never says. Between the two errors, the passage always wins: when a detail cannot be found on a second look, the honest fix is to answer the part that is supported and mark the rest, not to invent the missing half.

learn.title: A practice passage to read as if unseen

blocks.text: पिछले महीने हमारे विद्यालय में तीन दिन की पुस्तक-प्रदर्शनी लगी। सोमवार की सुबह प्रधानाचार्य जी ने इसका उद्घाटन किया। पुस्तकालय अध्यक्ष आदित्य ने बताया कि इस बार प्रदर्शनी में चार सौ पुस्तकें रखी गई थीं। इनमें से एक सौ बीस पुस्तकें विद्यार्थियों ने दान की थीं, और शेष पुस्तकालय की थीं। प्रदर्शनी का उद्देश्य सरल था — पढ़ने की आदत को बढ़ावा देना। प्रदर्शनी में विज्ञान, इतिहास और साहित्य की पुस्तकें अलग-अलग मेज़ों पर रखी गई थीं, और सबसे अधिक पुस्तकें कहानियों की मेज़ पर देखी गईं। पहले दिन कक्षा छह और सात के विद्यार्थी आए। दूसरे दिन कक्षा आठ और नौ के विद्यार्थियों ने प्रदर्शनी देखी। तीसरे दिन अभिभावक आए और शाम को प्रदर्शनी समाप्त हुई। शिक्षिका सुशीला जी ने बच्चों को समझाया कि पुस्तक खरीदना आवश्यक नहीं, पढ़ना आवश्यक है। उन्होंने यह भी बताया कि पुस्तकालय में नई पुस्तकें हर महीने आती हैं और विद्यार्थी उन्हें समय पर लौटा दें तो सबको पढ़ने का अवसर मिलता है। विद्यार्थियों ने अपने-अपने अनुभव लिखे और पर्चियाँ पुस्तकालय की पेटी में डालीं। पुस्तकालय प्रभारी ने बताया कि विद्यार्थियों की पर्चियों के आधार पर ही अगले महीने नई पुस्तकें मँगवाई जाएँगी। अभिभावकों ने प्रदर्शनी देखकर पुस्तकालय को दस नई पुस्तकें दान करने का भी वादा किया। तीन दिनों में विद्यार्थियों ने एक सौ पचास पुस्तकें उधार लीं और लगभग एक सौ विद्यार्थियों ने पुस्तकालय की सदस्यता ली। प्रधानाचार्य जी ने कहा कि अगले वर्ष से यह प्रदर्शनी हर तिमाही होगी।

items.text: प्रश्न: प्रदर्शनी का उद्देश्य क्या था? उत्तर: प्रदर्शनी का उद्देश्य पढ़ने की आदत को बढ़ावा देना था।
items.note: A factual answer taken from one stated line — a complete sentence, the passage’s wording kept, and nothing added.

items.text: प्रश्न: चार सौ पुस्तकों में से कितनी पुस्तकें विद्यार्थियों ने दान की थीं? उत्तर: विद्यार्थियों ने एक सौ बीस पुस्तकें दान की थीं।
items.note: A number answer copied exactly as printed — the figure, its unit and the doer of the action, with no rounding.

learn.title: Checking the answers against the passage

items: For every answer, point to the line it came from — if you cannot, the answer is from you rather than from the passage.
For every figure and name, compare with the printed original, including spelling, character by character.
Read every sentence once as Hindi — complete, agreed, in the tense the question implies.
Count the parts of every multi-part question against the parts you answered, in the order asked.
Confirm every summary contains who, what and result, and drops only the decoration.
Leave a genuine attempt for every item rather than a blank — a supported partial answer is still an answer.

blocks.text: The check is the cheapest marks on this task, because the answers already exist and only accuracy is in question. Read each answer once against its line: students who do this catch a transposed figure, a name spelled from memory and a sentence that drifted into general knowledge — the three faults that cost this task most often. Then read the set as a whole: does every question asked have an answer written, in Hindi, at the depth asked? Practice builds the method faster than advice does: take a fresh 250-word passage, run the two reads, answer without looking back, then verify line by line and record which kind of error recurred. The passage will always be new; the checking habit is what makes the next one feel less so.

figures.caption: Figure: from first read to checked answer
figures.description: A four-stage horizontal flow: the passage shown with its opening sentences highlighted for the survey read; a question with its evidence line marked inside the passage; the answer sentence being written in Hindi; and an arrow returning from the answer to the marked line for the final check. The return arrow is drawn heavier than the forward arrows to show where most of the accuracy is won.

figures.caption: Figure: the four layers of a comprehension answer
figures.description: Four nested bands, outermost first: what the passage actually says; what the question asks of it — factual, reference, summary or inference; the complete Hindi sentence that carries the answer; and at the centre the single line of evidence that proves it. Each band is labelled, and small tick marks on the innermost band show answers that can be traced to a printed line.

keyPoints: The syllabus records a passage of about 250 words, answered in Hindi, testing understanding of its content.
The number of questions is not fixed in the 2028 syllabus text, so practise varied question forms rather than a count.
Two reads with different jobs: the first finds the shape of the passage, the second pins the evidence for each question.
Name the question type before answering — factual, vocabulary, reference, summary or inference each has its own discipline.
Answer from the passage only: take its wording, reshape it into a complete Hindi sentence, and change no fact.
Copy numbers, dates and names exactly as printed; nearly right is still wrong.
A summary keeps who, what and result and drops decoration; an inference never walks past what the passage supports.
Check every answer against the line it came from — the return trip is where this task’s marks are kept.
The practice passage on this page is original BoardPrep writing, so its answers can be verified against it line by line.
examFocus: Survey before detail: read the shape of the passage first so every question becomes a visit to one place, not a search.
Locate the evidence line before writing — an answer written first and checked later is an answer built twice.
Write complete Hindi sentences at the depth asked, with the passage’s facts and your own sentence structure.
Treat figures and names as exact strings: copy them from the page, never from memory or approximation.
For reference questions, restate the line in plainer Hindi from its context instead of quoting it back unchanged.
Use the final read to point every answer at its line — the commonest faults (figure, spelling, general knowledge) all surface there.

vocabulary.meaning: An unseen prose passage — one not read or prepared before.
vocabulary.context: Apathit gadya is the task the syllabus describes as a passage of about 250 words.

vocabulary.meaning: A fact — something explicitly stated rather than inferred.
vocabulary.context: Factual questions ask for the tathy exactly as the passage prints it.

vocabulary.meaning: The essence or summary of a longer piece of writing.
vocabulary.context: A saar question keeps who, what and result and drops the decoration.

vocabulary.meaning: The intended meaning of a sentence or expression in its context.
vocabulary.context: Asking what a line means is asking for its aashay in plainer words.

vocabulary.meaning: The context surrounding a word or statement.
vocabulary.context: The meaning of a word is fixed by its sandarbh in the passage.

vocabulary.meaning: An inference — what follows from the passage without being stated outright.
vocabulary.context: An anuman must stay inside what the passage supports, or it becomes a guess.

vocabulary.meaning: The meaning of a word as it is used, which may differ from its general sense.
vocabulary.context: Answer a shabdarth question from the sentence the word sits in.

vocabulary.meaning: A second, targeted reading after the initial survey of the passage.
vocabulary.context: The punah-path is where each question’s evidence line gets marked.

questions.prompt: According to the syllabus statement recorded for this subject, how long is the unseen passage?
questions.explanation: The syllabus statement records a passage of about 250 words. Practising with passages of that length is therefore practice at the real scale of the task, including the timing of two full reads.
questions.commonMistake: Practising only short two-line extracts, then finding the real passage runs far longer than the habit prepared for.

questions.prompt: In which language are the answers to the unseen passage written?
questions.explanation: The syllabus statement says the questions are answered in Hindi to test understanding of the content, so both the understanding and its expression belong to this task — an answer in another language answers only half of it.
questions.commonMistake: Thinking the answers may be written in any language — the statement is explicit about Hindi.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a factual question about a passage?
options: What was the stated purpose of the exhibition?
What does the author imply about society?
How does the passage make you feel?
What would have happened if the exhibition had failed?
questions.answer: What was the stated purpose of the exhibition?
questions.explanation: A factual question asks for something the passage states directly, and the stated purpose is printed in one line of the practice passage. The other three ask for feelings, implications or counterfactuals that the passage does not settle.
questions.commonMistake: Answering an inference question with general knowledge — the test is what this passage states, not what is generally true.

questions.prompt: प्रदर्शनी में कुल कितनी पुस्तकें रखी गई थीं?
questions.explanation: The practice passage states four hundred books were placed in all, with one hundred twenty donated by students and one hundred fifty borrowed during the three days — three different figures that each answer a different question.
questions.commonMistake: Picking the figure that was read most recently rather than the one the question asks for: the total placed, not the donated or borrowed numbers.

questions.prompt: Complete: the 2028 syllabus text does not fix the number of ________ , and the answers are written in ________ .
questions.explanation: The statement fixes the passage length and the answer language but not how many questions follow, which is why practice must cover varied question forms rather than one repeated count.
questions.commonMistake: Preparing for a fixed number of questions and losing confidence when a different count appears on the paper.

questions.prompt: What should the first reading of an unseen passage do, and what should it avoid doing?
questions.answer: The first reading should establish the shape: what the passage is about, how it is organised, where the facts and figures sit, and where it begins and ends — enough to anchor every later search. It should stop short of hunting for detail, because chasing individual facts before the shape is known turns every question into a fresh reading of the whole page and spends the time the second read needed.
questions.explanation: The question asks for both halves of the discipline, and the second half is where the marks are: saying what the survey read is for, and why detail-reading first costs time twice.
questions.commonMistake: Describing only what to do on the first read without saying what it must avoid — the contrast is the method.

questions.prompt: From the practice passage: how many books did the students donate, and how many belonged to the library?
questions.answer: विद्यार्थियों ने एक सौ बीस पुस्तकें दान की थीं। प्रदर्शनी में कुल चार सौ पुस्तकें रखी गई थीं, इसलिए शेष दो सौ अस्सी पुस्तकें पुस्तकालय की थीं।
questions.explanation: The donated figure is printed directly; the library’s share is the remainder of the stated total, so the answer combines one printed fact with one subtraction the passage itself invites — four hundred minus one hundred twenty.
questions.commonMistake: Quoting the donated figure and stopping, when the question asks for both groups and the second is derivable from the total.

questions.prompt: Answer in Hindi from the practice passage: प्रदर्शनी के तीनों दिन किस-किस ने देखा, और समापन पर क्या हुआ?
questions.answer: पहले दिन कक्षा छह और सात के विद्यार्थी आए। दूसरे दिन कक्षा आठ और नौ के विद्यार्थियों ने प्रदर्शनी देखी। तीसरे दिन अभिभावक आए और उसी दिन शाम को प्रदर्शनी समाप्त हुई। समापन पर प्रधानाचार्य जी ने कहा कि अगले वर्ष से यह प्रदर्शनी हर तिमाही होगी, और तीन दिनों में विद्यार्थियों ने एक सौ पचास पुस्तकें उधार ली थीं।
questions.explanation: The question has three parts — the visitors of each of the three days, the closing event and what accompanied it — so the answer keeps them in order and draws every item from a stated line: the three day sentences, the evening closure, the principal’s closing remark and the borrowings figure.
questions.commonMistake: Answering only the three visitor groups and omitting the closure, because a multi-part question awards part by part and an omitted part has no answer at all.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between a factual answer and a summary answer, showing one of each from the practice passage.
questions.answer: A factual answer takes one stated detail and gives it exactly: asked for the purpose of the exhibition, it returns that the purpose was to encourage the habit of reading — the line the passage prints, complete in a sentence and with nothing around it. A summary answer compresses several stated details into one sentence that keeps who, what and result: summarising the exhibition, it would say that a three-day book exhibition of four hundred books was held in the school, visited class-wise by students and then by parents, during which one hundred fifty books were borrowed and a quarterly exhibition was announced for the future. The factual answer is a single point copied faithfully; the summary is the skeleton of several paragraphs held together with the decoration removed.
questions.explanation: The contrast is precision against compression: one detail exactly as stated versus the load-bearing facts of many. Giving one of each from the same passage shows the difference in operation rather than in definition.
questions.commonMistake: Turning the factual answer into a mini-summary by adding context the question did not ask for.

questions.prompt: A student copies four consecutive lines from the passage for every question. Comment on this approach and show how you would answer differently.
questions.answer: The approach has one merit and two costs. The merit is that a copied passage invents nothing, so nothing false is added. The first cost is that copying answers the passage rather than the question: a question about the purpose arrives wrapped in the sentences around the purpose, and the reader must find your answer inside your answer. The second cost is time — four lines per question, multiplied across the set, consumes the minutes the checking pass needed, and because the evidence was never located deliberately it is also the slowest way to find it. The better method is evidence first, sentence second: name the question’s type, mark the line that settles it, then write a complete Hindi sentence that carries the passage’s wording in your own structure — that the purpose of the exhibition was to encourage the habit of reading — and finally return to the line to verify each figure or name. That keeps the accuracy of copying while showing the understanding the task is built to test.
questions.explanation: A comment must weigh rather than merely condemn: the copied answer is safe but unfocused and slow, and the replacement method has to be demonstrated, not asserted. Working one question through the better method turns the criticism into evidence that you can answer differently.
questions.commonMistake: Rejecting copying outright without acknowledging why students use it — the answer that persuades explains what the habit gets right before showing what it costs.
